1.text: their name, Aiˊwan, was used among reindeer-breeders as an expression of

2.text: contempt. With the coming of American whalers, however, Eskimo traders

3.text: came into possession of so many things necessary or tempting to the Reindeer

4.text: people, that they could no longer be despised. With their increased trading

5.text: capacity, their demand for Chukchee reindeer is much greater than ever.

6.text: Every fall the squadron of Indian Point skin boats and whale-boats returns

7.text: from St. Lawrence Bay or from Holy Cross Bay, where the Reindeer people

8.text: are numerous, deeply laden with skins and meat, part of which is bartered

9.text: off to the Eskimo of St. Lawrence Island for whale-skin and blubber.
